newsitem.title: INDIA: India expects enough wheat stocks in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: India expects enough wheat stocks in 1997/98.

text.p: India, forced to import wheat in 1996/97 to boost stocks, expects to buy enough this year to avert a crisis and raise government inventories, officials and analysts said on Tuesday.
"The wheat front is good this year. There is good procurement," M.S. Bhatia, economic advisor in the Agriculture Ministry, told Reuters.
Bhatia said the Food Ministry was expecting to procure up to 10 million tonnes of wheat in the 1997/98 (April-March) marketing year.
"Even if it is not procured it is available in the market," he said.
The Indian government buys wheat to build up its buffer stocks, which it then uses to control prices by releasing stocks through a state-run distribution system.
The Agriculture Ministry has put the 1996/97 (July-June) wheat crop at 64.5 million tonnes against 62.6 million in 1995/96. India produced 65.47 million tonnes of wheat in 1994/95.
Government procurement in the 1995/96 wheat year fell to 8.2 million tonnes from 12.3 million tonnes in the previous year due to a three-million-tonne shortfall in production.

Officials of the state-run Food Corporation of India (FCI), the largest grain trading agency, said that until Saturday, FCI had procured 6.5 million tonnes of wheat compared with seven million tonnes procured at the same time last year.
Officials said procurement, which usually tapers off by the middle of May, was expected to last until June 10 this year since harvesting began late due to a prolonged winter.
The official said procurement was virtually at its peak and state agencies were buying about 350,000 tonnes of wheat daily.
A threat by farmers not to sell their produce to the government if state-fixed prices were not hiked also delayed procurements.
Under the government's buffer stock objectives, India must hold 13.1 million tonnes of wheat and 9.2 million tonnes of rice as on July 1 every year.
FCI officials said they were optimistic of meeting the target this year with steady procurement and arrivals of imported wheat.

S.M. Virmani, an agriculture expert with the Hyderabad-based International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT), said while it was very hard to estimate government wheat purchases, the situation was expected to be comfortable.
In December, India authorised the state-run State Trading Corporation (STC) to import two million tonnes of wheat to build stocks and check rising prices.
STC officials said their organisation had contracted to import 2.7 million tonnes of wheat since December 1996. Of this, 1.7 million tonnes had been contracted by March 31 this year.
The government announced fresh import of two million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98 (April-March) of which STC has contracted for one million.
